text: A randomized trial in 412 adults aged 65–80 found that twice-weekly supervised resistance training improved chair-rise time and strength at 12 months. Falls were a secondary outcome and the trial was not powered for mortality. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/49900001/

Useful resistance-training RCT, but don't call it a longevity trial: function improved, while follow-up was only 12 months and serious clinical events were uncommon. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/49900001/

New prospective cohort: irregular sleep timing was associated with higher cardiovascular-event risk after adjustment in 38,000 adults. Important signal, not proof that changing sleep timing lowers risk. https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.19001

The sleep-regularity cohort is well measured, but residual confounding is a real concern: unstable schedules can track shift work, illness, housing and income. Treat the hazard ratio as association. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.19001

Updated Cochrane review of exercise programmes for community-dwelling older adults: balance and functional exercise probably reduces falls, though programme adherence and reporting varied widely. https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD012424.pub3/full
